findings.description: Critical: New-roadmap candidate intake never specifies how required roadmap envelope fields are derived. design.md says intake feeds validate/save/scaffold, but roadmap.schema.json requires roadmap_id and source_proposal, and neither the D5 mapping table nor the Candidate intake section defines those values for stub-originated roadmaps.
findings.resolution: Extend the intake contract and roadmap-orchestration scenarios to state exact derivation rules for roadmap_id and source_proposal (and any other envelope fields required by validate/save/scaffold), including operator-provided versus stub-derived sources.

findings.description: Nit: Bug-scrub eligibility is contradictory across the plan. D3 and the skill-workflow scenario speak of a promoted/eligible finding, while the refined producer contract requires emitting every finding already selected by the severity filter, and bug-scrub's default severity_filter is low.
findings.resolution: Pick one rule and use it everywhere: either define promoted/eligible as membership in the severity-filtered report set, or define a stricter promotion gate; update D3, the refined contract, and the Bug-scrub promotes a finding scenario to match.

findings.description: Nit: The bug-scrub category-to-effort table is not executable. design.md buckets simple diagnostics, test/deferred, and architecture/security/spec, but Finding.category also includes lint, type-error, and code-marker, which are never named in the mapping.
findings.resolution: Replace the prose buckets with an explicit category→effort table covering every Finding.category value, and add a fail-closed rule for any unexpected category.

findings.description: Nit: The inert-rendering / opaque-provenance security rule exists only in design.md and is absent from the skill-workflow and roadmap-orchestration spec deltas, so it is not a testable requirement for implementers or validators.
findings.resolution: Add a SHALL requirement and scenario that candidate title/description/rationale/provenance are treated as inert data: renderers escape structure and must not dereference provenance URIs.

findings.description: Nit: Explore-feature mapping says it maps blockers, but neither design.md nor the Explore-feature emits shortlist candidates scenario states whether opportunities.json blocked_by entries become candidate-work depends_on, tags, or are dropped.
findings.resolution: Specify a deterministic blocked_by→depends_on (or explicit non-mapping) rule, including how non-change-id blocker strings are rejected or encoded.

findings.description: Nit: tasks.md Phase 1 implementation tasks depend only on their RED tests and omit 0.2, even though producer adapters need the shared validator/atomic writer created in 0.2; work-packages.yaml currently carries that ordering instead.
findings.resolution: Add task 0.2 to the Dependencies lists for tasks 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6 so the task graph matches the shared-module prerequisite already expressed by wp-producers→wp-contracts.

findings.description: Nit: wp-producers.write_allow includes skills/tests/bug-scrub/**, but its verification command runs only skills/bug-scrub/tests and omits skills/tests/bug-scrub, so documentation-contract updates in the canonical test tree would not be exercised by the package gate.
findings.resolution: Extend the Producer suites pass command to include skills/tests/bug-scrub, matching the write scope and the explore-feature dual-tree pattern already present.

findings.description: Optional: Failure semantics define user-facing refusals, but the plan adds no structured logging, stable error codes, or metrics for sidecar validation failures, mixed-batch ranking refusals, or intake collision/dependency failures.
findings.resolution: Accept for this CLI-skill migration, or optionally require machine-readable error codes plus one structured log/event per refused write/rank/intake path.

findings.description: Optional: If emit-every-severity-filtered-finding remains the rule, default severity_filter=low can project very large candidate batches into prioritize-proposals with no plan-level bound, pagination, or higher candidate threshold.
findings.resolution: Accept if operators are expected to raise the filter, or document a candidate-specific minimum severity / max-batch guard before ranking.

findings.description: FYI: Ranking treats unresolved active dependencies as blocked queue entries, while intake fails closed on unresolved dependencies. That stage difference is coherent, but a one-line cross-reference in design.md would prevent implementers from unifying the two behaviors by mistake.
findings.resolution: No change required; optionally add an explicit note that ranking may soft-block while intake must hard-fail.

findings.description: The work-package DAG is acyclic, parallel packages have non-overlapping write scopes, wp-prioritize correctly waits on wp-producers, and roadmap-intake/integration deny openspec/roadmaps/** so active roadmap mutation stays outside package write scopes.
findings.resolution: Keep the validated package boundaries and roadmap deny lists as implementation invariants.

findings.description: Fail-closed persistence and mutation safety are well specified: full-batch validation before atomic sidecar replacement, no partial files, ranking refusal before scoring, and existing-roadmap changes only through refine-roadmap preview/apply.
findings.resolution: Preserve these refusal and transaction boundaries in shared writer and plan-roadmap intake tests.

findings.description: The additive-sidecar approach correctly preserves rich producer artifacts, keeps the improve-harness legacy proposal flag for one migration window, and leaves the ri-11 candidate-work schema unchanged while centralizing validation in skills/shared.
findings.resolution: Retain additive outputs and the compatibility wrapper through the stated migration window.
